clue.text: Lovers of the phonetic alphabet

parts.note: Shakespeare's star-crossed couple are both names of letters in the NATO alphabet, used for R and J

explanation.surface: Seems to describe enthusiasts for radio spelling codes.
explanation.walkthrough: The two famous lovers of the play share their names with the NATO code words for R and J, so 'of the phonetic alphabet' says where else they appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic young couple are literature's best-known pair of lovers.

clue.text: Frenetic head, storming around, looks like this?

indicators.note: storming about in a rage, the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An agitated boss stomps about, and we are asked what such a person's face looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storming around' rearranges FRENETICHEAD. The whole clue also paints the scene: a furious, frenetic head looks flushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flushed with anger or embarrassment has a reddened complexion, which is how a storming boss appears.

clue.text: Parrot beginning to make a sound like a crow

indicators.note: the beginning of the word make is its opening letter

parts.note: caw is the harsh call a crow makes

explanation.surface: A parrot starts to imitate a crow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large, brightly coloured tropical American species of parrot.

clue.text: Misaligned, hence moved to No 1 court?

definitions.meaning: not properly lined up, skewed from the middle
at Wimbledon a match shifted from Centre Court to No 1 Court has been taken ...

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon's main show court is Centre Court and the next is No 1 Court; a match moved there is 'off Centre'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misaligned sits away from its proper middle position.

clue.text: Surprisingly won seat, Labour not being involved

indicators.note: a surprising result jumbles the expected order of these letters

explanation.surface: An election upset: a seat won without the Labour Party standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges WONSEAT. 'Labour' looks like the British political party but means toil.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an easy task means no effort or toil was needed.

clue.text: Military doctrine, merely crude when raised

parts.note: merely and just both mean only

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a word reads it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: crude, unrefined material is raw

explanation.surface: Reads as a jibe that a military theory is simply primitive once brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when raised' turns RAW upwards into WAR in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethical theory setting out when armed conflict is morally justifiable is a doctrine about warfare.

clue.text: One twice disturbs Len in this relaxing morning

indicators.note: disturbing the letters shakes them out of their order
the single letter is used two times over

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone keeps waking Len during a lazy morning in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles I, and 'disturbs' rearranges IILEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy extra stretch in bed past the usual rising time makes a relaxing morning.

clue.text: Korean, for one, eats cooking by a Welsh girl

indicators.note: cooking works the letters of the word eats into a new form

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Korean eats food prepared by a woman from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges EATS as EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Korea lies in the far east of the Asian continent, so a Korean is an example of someone from there.

clue.text: Not hearing about cold drink

indicators.note: the word for not hearing goes around the other letter

parts.note: someone not hearing is deaf
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone fails to catch a request about an iced drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with the caffeine removed is a common drink ordered by that short name.

clue.text: Cliffhanging sort of account?

definitions.meaning: tense uncertainty over what happens next, as in a cliffhanger
in bookkeeping, a temporary account where entries wait until they can be allocated

explanation.definitionFit: A cliffhanger leaves an audience in tense anticipation, and accountants hold unallocated sums in a holding ledger of that name.

clue.text: Tweeter reviewed brewed lagers

indicators.note: viewed again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone posts online reviews of home-brewed beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges BREWEDLAGERS. 'Tweeter' suggests a social media user, but here it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: This reed-bed songbird of Europe chirps, so it is a tweeter in the bird sense.

clue.text: Finally arrived, but out of contention

definitions.meaning: split as two words it says at last present: at this moment in this place
a competitor placed far back is said to be absent from the reckoning

explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,4 the letters read as 'now here', someone who has finally arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who finishes far behind is described as having come absolutely last, out of contention.

clue.text: We must hold girl back at first, potential starlet

indicators.note: the outer word holds the others inside it

parts.note: taken as written
Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word back

explanation.surface: An instruction to restrain a young actress who is pushing forward too early.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiring hopeful who wants to become a star is someone who could one day be a starlet.

clue.text: Raise one in army

indicators.note: the single letter sits inside the word for an army

parts.note: host is an old word for an army, a great multitude
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Reads like an order to promote one soldier in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' as an army is an old sense, as in 'the heavenly host'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something up, often with ropes or tackle, is to raise it.

clue.text: On the way, carried by Ford?

definitions.meaning: the Ford Transit is a popular van, so goods carried in it are in one

explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Transit is a best-selling van in Britain, so the second reading means 'inside a Transit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods being conveyed and not yet delivered are said to be travelling, on their way.

clue.text: Object about ill-considered heavy defeat

indicators.note: the word for an object goes around the other piece

parts.note: an object is a thing
an ill-considered act is rash

explanation.surface: Someone protests against a hasty verdict after a crushing loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe beating in sport, winning by a wide margin, is a heavy defeat.

clue.text: Clog (old) deliberately ruined

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog
old means aged

explanation.surface: An old wooden shoe that someone has wrecked on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is said to come from workers throwing sabots into machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate destruction or obstruction, often of machinery, is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: The dafter sort of sitcom?

indicators.note: to sort letters is to arrange them afresh

explanation.surface: A question about which sitcom is the sillier kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges THEDAFTER. The comedy is a 1990s Channel 4 sitcom about priests on an Irish island.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a much-loved Irish-set television situation comedy.

clue.text: Poet's title so unusual

definitions.note: read as 'poet is', so the definition is the poet

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of these letters gives a new order

explanation.surface: A poet's honorific is described as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TITLESO; 'Poet's' is 'poet is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Waste Land is one of the major modernist poets.

clue.text: Doctor to consume fluid and toast

indicators.note: the outer letters take the fluid inside them

parts.note: ink is a writing fluid

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to drink liquid and eat toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like bread but is the verb: to raise a glass to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising glasses in someone's honour is to toast them.

clue.text: Already told not to delay purchase

indicators.note: told signals that the phrase is said out loud

parts.note: an urging to shop at once is 'buy now'

explanation.surface: A shopper says they were already urged not to wait before buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something should have happened at this point means it should have happened already.

clue.text: Care had to be exercised in this absurd pretence

indicators.note: exercised means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that care is needed amid a farcical sham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be exercised' rearranges CAREHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty show put on to keep up appearances is called a farce or travesty.

clue.text: Some virtual example of personal assistant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describes something as an instance of a digital assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'of' into the definition; 'of' is only a link, so the definition is 'personal assistant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazon's voice-controlled helper is a virtual personal assistant.

clue.text: Italian team keeping on leader of chant

indicators.note: the club's name keeps the other word inside it

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club

explanation.surface: An Italian football club retains the chap who starts their chants.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter is Internazionale, the Milan football club.
explanation.definitionFit: In church, the person who sings the opening words of a chant leads it.

clue.text: Never ever green, even vaguely? That's primarily desert

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A land never even vaguely green is mostly desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The arid region in southern Israel is a desert.

clue.text: Mark that may be one over the 8?

definitions.text: Mark that may be one over the 8?

parts.words: Mark that may be one over the 8?
parts.note: on a keyboard the star symbol sits above the figure 8 key; 'one over the eight' is also slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Seems to describe someone a drink too many, 'one over the eight' being British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The star-shaped typographic mark is printed on the 8 key, over the digit.

clue.text: Russian author left by such an erotic dancer

parts.note: a go-go dancer performs in clubs

explanation.surface: A Russian writer is abandoned by an exotic dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb (abandoned) but is L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai, author of Dead Souls and The Overcoat, was a Russian writer.

clue.text: Our narrow separation from the EU

definitions.text: Our narrow separation from the EU

parts.words: Our narrow separation from the EU
parts.note: the narrow sea channel between England and France, which can also read as a slim Brexit vote

explanation.surface: Seems to be about Britain's narrow Brexit vote to leave the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrowest stretch of the English Channel divides Britain from France, an EU country.
